comparison: Both evaluations support the iSAM system development (C1, C8, C9, C62-C66). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation across multiple cell types with dose-response data. Peer reviewers praised the system as 'very useful' and 'very versatile,' characterizing it as 'well-characterised.' OpenEval also covers sodium butyrate rescue (C54-C61) which peer reviewers address separately in R9.

Perfect agreement on gene identification strategy (C2, C7, C35, C36, C38). Both evaluations support the comparative scRNAseq analysis and candidate gene identification. OpenEval details the methodology and datasets used, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted the approach as part of 'solid data analysis.'

Divergent evaluations of arterial cell expansion claims (C3, C10, C50-C53). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising critical concern about whether results stem from 'simultaneous activation of all 9 TF or just a subset,' undermining attribution to collective action.

OpenEval supports colony-forming assay results (C11, C33) showing differential effects on colony types with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN rating for overlapping claims reflects the same concern about pooled activation—whether observed effects result from all nine factors or a subset.

Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN the mechanistic link between RUNX1T1 and IGFBP2 (C12-C14). OpenEval notes the causal link is 'speculative and based on correlation' with absent direct mechanistic validation. Peer reviewers express the same concern about pooled activation making it unclear which factors drive IGFBP2 upregulation.

Strong agreement on IGFBP2 functional effects (C15-C17, C19, C21). OpenEval supports claims with colony-forming assays and flow cytometry showing distinct mechanisms. Peer reviewers 'exhaustively demonstrated' endorsement strongly validates IGFBP2's role in promoting hematopoietic progenitors. Peer R5 also includes C22 which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Both support IGFBP2 expression patterns in AGM niche (C20, C40). OpenEval validates using published in vivo scRNAseq data and in vitro data. Peer reviewers accepted these expression observations as supporting biological relevance without challenge.

Both support temporal specificity and endothelial cluster characterization (C23-C26, C30). OpenEval details time-course scRNAseq showing day 13 specificity with coordinated marker changes. Peer reviewers' 'exhaustive demonstration' statement encompasses these mechanistic findings about IGFBP2's effects, which are temporally linked to these observations.

Both support metabolic profiling data (C27-C29, C34). OpenEval validates metabolic shift with KEGG analysis, Seahorse measurements, and gene expression. Peer reviewers' endorsement of 'exhaustive demonstration' and 'solid data analysis' encompasses these mechanistic findings about IGFBP2's metabolic effects.

Perfect agreement on cell cycle analysis (C31-C32). Both support the finding that IGFBP2 acts during cell fate specification rather than proliferation. OpenEval details DAPI staining and flow cytometry evidence. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of the 'exhaustive demonstration' of IGFBP2's mechanism.

Both support sorted cell population experiments (C18) showing relationship between arterial identity and progenitor potential. OpenEval notes this provides important context for EHT interpretation. Peer reviewers accepted this observation as aligning with overall findings about cell populations.

Perfect agreement on established literature claims (C5, C6, C37, C39, C41, C43-C46, C61). Both evaluations support these as appropriately cited background facts. OpenEval notes citations appear accurate and relevant. Peer reviewers did not challenge any contextual claims. OpenEval also includes C54 which peer reviewers address in R9.

Both support speculative mechanistic interpretation about RUNX1T1 lacking DNA binding domain (C42). OpenEval notes this demonstrates appropriate scientific caution about mechanism needing elucidation. Peer reviewers accepted this as reasonable inference from structural properties. OpenEval R13 also covers C36, C48-C49 addressed elsewhere by peer reviewers.

Both support acknowledgment of technical limitations (C49). OpenEval notes this demonstrates appropriate scientific caution about pooled approach constraints. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged the same limitation that 'it is not always clear whether the observed results were the consequence of the simultaneous activation of all 9 TF or just a subset.'

Both support the methodological conclusion about integrated approach (C47, C48). OpenEval rates as reasonable but notes broader validation would strengthen the claim. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed versatility and broad applicability, stating the system 'appears to be very versatile and applicable to a broad variety of studies.'

Peer reviewers separately evaluated transgene silencing and sodium butyrate solution (C54-C60) as SUPPORTED, characterizing the technical approach as 'well-characterised.' OpenEval addresses these claims within R1 as part of comprehensive iSAM system validation.

OpenEval R3 includes pan-endothelial marker expression (C52) as part of arterial cell expansion validation. Peer reviewers separately evaluated C52 as SUPPORTED in R15, noting this represents standard marker analysis consistent with known EHT biology.
